6.title: Clients
6.content: Structure of a client and the options of pankosmia_metadata.json .

7.title: Table of Contents
7.content: . | What is a client | Structure of a client | pankosmia_metadata.json . | Examples | . | endpoints | .

8.title: What is a client
8.content: A client is a web app (React, built with Vite) served by the Pankosmia server at /clients/<name>. The dashboard, the settings and every content handler (core-contenthandler_*) are clients. A product includes a client by listing it in CLIENTn in app_config.env (and so in libClients of buildSpec.json). The build then copies its build/ output, package.json, pankosmia_metadata.json and storage_id.json (when it exists) into lib/clients/<repository name>.

9.title: Structure of a client
9.content: | Item | What it does | . | pankosmia_metadata.json | Declares the client to the server and the other clients (see below). | . | package.json | Dependencies and scripts. homepage is /clients/<name>. | . | vite.config.js | Vite setup: base is /clients/<name>/, the dev server has its own port, and /api is proxied to the Pankosmia server (port 19119). | . | index.html, public/ | Page shell and static files. | . | src/index.jsx | Entry point. It wraps the app in the RCL SpSpa component with requireNet, titleKey (pages:<id>:title) and currentId (the metadata id). | . | src/App.jsx, src/components/ | The pages and components of the client. | . | build/ | Output of vite build, the folder the server actually serves. | . | storage_id.json | A generated UUID of the client (written by scripts/write-storage-id.js before start, dev and build), when the client uses it. | .

10.title: pankosmia_metadata.json
10.content: This file is the identity card of a client. The server reads it to list the client (/api/list-clients) and to publish what it can do (/api/client-interfaces), and the translations it contains feed the i18n tree. Fields: . | Field | Type | What it does | . | id | string | Unique identifier of the client. It is the section name in the i18n tree (pages:<id>:...), the currentId given to SpSpa, and it identifies the client in the menu. | . | require.net | boolean | When true, the client needs internet. Its menu entry is disabled while the app is offline, and a page using requireNet shows a “no entry if offline” message. | . | require.debug | boolean | When true, the client is a developer tool: it is listed in the Debug section of the menu, which only appears when debug mode is on. When false or absent, the client is in the normal menu. | . | minServerVersion | string | Minimum server version (for example 0.20.3). The app does not run if the server is older than the minimum required by a client. | . | exclude_from_menu | boolean | When true, the client is not listed in the menu of the header. It is still reachable by its URL and from links of other clients. | . | exclude_from_dashboard | boolean | When true, the client is removed from the dashboard, for example its entry in the Create button. | . | i18n | object | Translations of the client. Each key is a name with one text per language code. title and summary are conventional. See the i18n page. | . | endpoints | object | The actions the client offers to other clients, per document type (see below). | . Examples . The settings client is hidden from both the menu and the dashboard: . { "id": "core-settings", "require": { "net": false }, "minServerVersion": "0.20.3", "exclude_from_menu": true, "exclude_from_dashboard": true, "i18n": { "title": { "en": "Settings", "fr": "Paramètres" } } } . A content handler for developers only (require.debug), shown in the Debug section of the menu: . { "id": "contenthandler-template", "require": { "net": false, "debug": true }, "i18n": { "title": { "en": "contenthandler-template" } } } .

11.title: endpoints
11.content: Content handlers use endpoints to tell the other clients what they can do with a type of document (a flavor such as textTranslation). Other clients read it from /api/client-interfaces and build their menus from it, so a handler does not need to be known by name. Each action is a list of entries (edit is a single entry) with these fields: . | doc: a developer description of the entry. | label: an i18n key (for example pages:core-contenthandler_obs:create_content_obs) shown to the user. | url: the page of the client to open, relative to /clients/<id>/. | placeHolders: documents the variables used in url, such as %%REPO_PATH%%, replaced by the path of the repository in <X>/<Y>/<Z> format. | subMenu: only for export, groups the entries by format (usfm, pdf…). | . Actions in use: . | Action | Used for | . | create_document | Entries of the Create button of the dashboard. | . | edit | The client that opens a repository of this document type. | . | new_book, import_book, delete_book | Actions on a repository, offered in the Content client. | . | export | Export formats of a repository, per format in subMenu. | . | about_repo, manager, initDocument, importContent | Other entries read by the dashboard. | . | download_resources | Page used to download resources (remote repos client). | . { "id": "core-contenthandler_obs", "endpoints": { "textStories": { "create_document": [ { "doc": "Create a document for OBS", "label": "pages:core-contenthandler_obs:create_content_obs", "url": "/createDocument/obsContent" } ], "edit": { "doc": "main page for workspace", "label": "pages:core-client-workspace:main", "url": "core-local-workspace#" } } } } .

14.title: Knip
14.content: Knip is useful towards identifying unlisted dependencies, duplicated exports, and potential unused files, dependencies or exports. Watch out for false positives! . Avoid blindly implementing everything reported. Look, verify, and test. Do your own searches and thinking for things like reported unused exports. Knip is not meant for resource-core, webfonts-core, pankosmia-web, or desktop-app-*. It is for projects constructed with a packages.json and an index.js, which it uses to step through and evaluate all includes in the app. Setup . npm install -g knip or npm install --global knip (to install or update) . Analyzing a repo . In the root of the client repo in a terminal, enter knip. It will provide a list of any of any unused, unlisted, or duplicated things that it suspects it has found. Example of false positives on unused exports . It will report Selection.styles.jsx as an unused export (because of the filename) even when it is in use. Be careful to not remove this file where its export is actually in use. Example of reported duplicated exports not actually causing a problem . Selection.styles.jsx is exporting sx, which works fine as used. Example of false positive on unused dependencies . Knip is quite good at following the include chain throughout a project. However, sometimes dependencies are in place outside of this chain, which it will miss. For example, if a package.json includes use of react-scripts in its scripts section, it’s dependency chain includes babel which includes a devDependency of @babel/plugin-proposal-private-property-in-object. Knip will miss that case and report that as an unused dependency, but in that case it is actually used.

18.title: PanBasicDialog
18.content: A modal dialog sized to its content (minimum width 280px, maximum width sm). It shows a title, your content, and a row of action buttons at the bottom. It is the right choice for confirmations and short forms. Clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape calls closeFn. The dialog surface is rendered as an HTML form element. | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | . | titleLabel | string | required | Text shown as the dialog title. Translate it before passing it in. | . | isOpen | boolean | required | Whether the dialog is visible. The parent component owns this state. | . | closeFn | () => void | required | Function called to close the dialog. It is called when the user clicks the backdrop or presses Escape. Your code should use it to set isOpen to false. | . | children | ReactNode | none | The content of the dialog: any React nodes (text, form fields, lists…). | . | actionsButtonArray | ReactElement[] | none | Array of buttons rendered in the footer, in order. Normally the result of PanDialogActionsArray(...), but any array of React elements works. | . | requiredFieldsLabel | boolean | false | When true, a note is shown above the content explaining that required fields are marked (translation key library:pankosmia-rcl:required_field). Use it when the dialog contains a form with required fields. | . | dividers | boolean | false | When true, a horizontal divider is drawn between the title and the content, and between the content and the buttons. | .

19.title: PanAdvancedDialog
19.content: A modal dialog with a colored title bar (primary theme color), full width up to the sm breakpoint, and a divider above the buttons. It is meant for longer content and forms. Behavior on small screens . Below the sm breakpoint the dialog goes full screen. A close icon appears at the start of the title bar and calls closeFn. The footer is hidden, and the second button of actionsButtonArray (the action button created by PanDialogActionsArray) is moved to the end of the title bar. Keep the main action in second position so that it stays reachable on mobile. Unlike PanBasicDialog, clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape does not close this dialog. | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | . | titleLabel | string | required | Text shown as the dialog title. Translate it before passing it in. | . | isOpen | boolean | required | Whether the dialog is visible. The parent component owns this state. | . | closeFn | () => void | required | Function called when the user clicks the close icon shown in the title bar on small screens. Your code should use it to set isOpen to false. It is not called from the backdrop or Escape. | . | children | ReactNode | none | The content of the dialog: any React nodes (text, form fields, lists…). | . | actionsButtonArray | ReactElement[] | none | Array of buttons rendered in the footer, in order. Normally the result of PanDialogActionsArray(...), but any array of React elements works. | . | requiredFieldsLabel | boolean | false | When true, a note is shown above the content explaining that required fields are marked (translation key library:pankosmia-rcl:required_field). Use it when the dialog contains a form with required fields. | .

20.title: PanDialogActionsArray
20.content: Despite its name it is a plain function, not a component: call it like PanDialogActionsArray({ ... }). It returns an array of two elements, [closeButton, actionButton], to pass to the actionsButtonArray prop of PanBasicDialog or PanAdvancedDialog. The close button is always first. The action button is second; when onlyCloseButton is true that slot is null. | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | . | actionFn | () => void | required | Function run when the action button is clicked. Not used when onlyCloseButton is true. | . | actionLabel | string | required | Label of the action button. Translate it before passing it in. | . | closeFn | () => void | required | Function run when the close button is clicked. It is also called after actionFn when closeOnAction is true. | . | closeLabel | string | required | Label of the close button (for example Cancel or Close). Translate it before passing it in. | . | isDisabled | boolean | none | When true, the action button is disabled. Typically used while a form is invalid. The close button is never disabled by this prop. | . | closeOnAction | boolean | true | When true, closeFn is called right after actionFn. Set it to false when the action is asynchronous or can fail and your code must close the dialog itself. | . | onlyCloseButton | boolean | false | When true, only the close button is created (for information-only dialogs). The second array slot is null. | . | actionVariant | string | none | MUI Button variant of the action button: text, outlined or contained. When omitted, MUI’s default (text) is used. | . | closeVariant | string | none | MUI Button variant of the close button: text, outlined or contained. When omitted, MUI’s default (text) is used. | . | isLoading | boolean | none | When true, the close button is disabled and shows a small spinner. Note that this is applied to the close button only, not to the action button. | . | loadingLabel | string | none | Label that replaces the close button label while isLoading is true. If omitted, the normal label stays. | .

21.title: Examples
21.content: A dialog with a confirm action. The same pattern works for PanAdvancedDialog: . const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); <PanBasicDialog titleLabel="Delete this item?" isOpen={open} closeFn={() => setOpen(false)} actionsButtonArray={PanDialogActionsArray({ actionLabel: "Delete", actionFn: () => deleteItem(), closeLabel: "Cancel", closeFn: () => setOpen(false), actionVariant: "contained", })} > <Typography>This cannot be undone.</Typography> </PanBasicDialog> . Working demos are in src/componentDemos/V1.0 of the core-client-rcl repository.

28.title: i18n
28.content: How translation of the user interface works across all clients .

29.title: Table of Contents
29.content: . | Overview | Structure of the translation tree | Where the strings come from | How a client loads the translations | Using translations in code | Adding a string to a client | Localization Editor | Product-level customization | .

30.title: Overview
30.content: Every piece of user-interface text in Pankosmia is looked up by a key in one shared translation tree, so all clients (dashboard, settings, content handlers…) follow the same language. A key has three parts joined by colons: <category>:<section>:<name>, for example pages:core-settings:title. The value behind a key holds one translation per language code (en, fr, es, id…). When a key is not found, the key itself is displayed.

31.title: Structure of the translation tree
31.content: | Category | Content | . | pages | One section per client, named after the client id, filled from the i18n object of its pankosmia_metadata.json. Example: pages:core-settings:title. | . | library | Strings of shared libraries such as the RCL. Example: library:pankosmia-rcl:required_field. | . | components | Strings of shared interface parts (header, framework messages…). Example: components:framework:no_entry_if_offline. | . | branding | Identity of the product. Example: branding:software:name. | . | scripture | Names of books and versifications. | . | munchers, crunchers, flavors, server, fonts | Other categories of the template, used by specific content handlers and server features. | .

32.title: Where the strings come from
32.content: . | The template: the base file i18n.json of resource-core/templates. The desktop app build copies it to lib/templates/i18n.json. It holds library, components, branding, scripture… | Each client: the i18n object of its pankosmia_metadata.json. A key title in the client core-settings becomes pages:core-settings:title. | The product: i18nPatch.json and i18n-overrides.json in the globalBuildResources of the desktop app (see below). | .

33.title: How a client loads the translations
33.content: When a client starts, the SpSpa component of the RCL requests /api/i18n/flat from the server and keeps the result in the i18n context. The response is a flat map of key to text, for the language chosen by the user in the Settings client (stored through /api/settings/languages). Components read it with i18nRef.current and look up a key with doI18n.

34.title: Using translations in code
34.content: Both functions come from pankosmia-lib/i18n. doI18n(key, source) returns the text, or the key itself when it is missing. doInterpolatedI18n(key, values, source) fills the placeholders %1%, %2%… of a text with an array of strings. import { useContext } from "react"; import { i18nContext } from "pankosmia-rcl"; import { doI18n, doInterpolatedI18n } from "pankosmia-lib/i18n"; const { i18nRef } = useContext(i18nContext); doI18n("pages:core-settings:title", i18nRef.current); // "greeting": { "en": "Hello %1%, you have %2% books" } doInterpolatedI18n( "pages:my-client:greeting", ["Ada", "3"], i18nRef.current, ); . doInterpolatedI18n is stricter than doI18n: it throws when the key is missing, when a value is not a string, when the number of values differs from the number of placeholders, or when a placeholder is malformed.

41.title: Philosophy
41.content: Pankosmia began with a conversation about the First the monkey principle. TLDR, if your project is to have a monkey recite Shakespeare on a pedestal, don’t focus on the pedestal. In other words, tackle the hard bit first. For us, two of the hard bits were graphite support and guaranteeing an offline-first experience where failing to do so may put people in danger. Some corollaries of “First the Monkey” for us are: . | focus on the hard and unsolved problems | the working but clunky solution we can build and ship is better than both the lovely solution we can’t build and ship and the lovely UI we can ship that doesn’t do the right thing under the hood | polishing things that we know how to polish is rarely urgent | users need happy devs because devs build the systems the users need | .

67.title: PanMenuWrapper
67.content: A responsive wrapper around a list of menu items. It chooses the presentation from the screen size and renders your children inside it: . | From the sm breakpoint up: a standard MUI Menu popup anchored to anchorEl (internal component PanMenu). | Below sm: a swipeable drawer sliding up from the bottom of the screen with a drag handle, where the children are placed in a MenuList (internal component PanMenuDrawer). anchorEl is ignored. | . PanMenu and PanMenuDrawer are implementation details and are not exported; use PanMenuWrapper. | Prop | Type | Default | What it does | . | isOpen | boolean | required | Whether the menu (or drawer) is visible. The parent component owns this state. | . | setIsOpen | (open: boolean) => void | required | State setter called with false when the user dismisses the menu (clicking outside, pressing Escape, or swiping the drawer down). Your code is responsible for opening it again. | . | anchorEl | HTMLElement | none | The DOM element the popup is positioned next to, usually the button that opened it (event.currentTarget). Only used on larger screens. | . | children | ReactNode | none | The menu entries, typically MUI MenuItem elements (with ListItemIcon and ListItemText) and Dividers. | .

68.title: Examples
